summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Berlin under Hegel, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held an extraordinariat at Halle-Wittenberg (1831) before succeeding Johann Friedrich Herbart to a chair and rectorate at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Schenkl worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, studying at the University of Vienna and under Georg Curtius. He was a professor of classical philology at Innsbruck (1857–1864) and Graz (1864–1875), and later professor at Vienna (1875–1899).

Karl Schönfeld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Neuchâtel, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Zurich under doctoral supervisor Adolf Kaegi. He taught at Kantonsschule Rychenberg from 1905 to 1928.
Karl Scriba, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, completed his PhD at the University of Würzburg under Julius Jolly by 1902. He also studied at the universities of Munich and Berlin.

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard and with August Leskien. He served as a librarian at Halle-Wittenberg and Saxony-Anhalt (~1876–1883) and became docent at Copenhagen in 1882.

Karl Vilhelm Zetterstéen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala under Herman Almkvist and Eduard Sachau. He served as docent in Semitic languages at Uppsala (1895) and Lund (1895–1904), and was professor of Oriental studies at Uppsala (1904–1931).
Karl von Hegel was a historian and archaeologist who held academic posts at the University of Rostock from around 1841 to 1856 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1856 to 1887.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at the University of Munich. His career included posts at Munich, the Ifo Institute, Munich School of Politics, and as professor at FH Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD from Bonn and completed his habilitation at Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as the main student of Anagarika Govinda, whom he succeeded in 1982.

Karl-Stéphan Bouthillette works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Munich (2015–2019), Laval (2019–2020), FWO (2019–2022), Manipal Academy of Higher Education (2023), and the University of Hong Kong (2026).
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She served at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and was Numata Professor at Hawaiʻi in 2023.

Karma Phuntsho is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Michael Aris, Richard Gombrich, and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding research posts at CNRS and the University of Cambridge.

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned degrees from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed her PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who served as abbot at Young Lamas Home School around 1962 and at Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery, also founding Kampo Gangra Drubgyud Ling and Tekchen Lekshay Ling.

Karma Ura is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology who studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.
Karmen Bašić was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Zagreb and served as Executive Director of the Open Society Institute Croatia from circa 1993 to 1999.

Karsé Kongtrul studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Khakyab Dorje, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö; he also taught Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karthigesu Indrapala is a historian and Indologist who studied at Jaffna College, the University of Ceylon, and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1961–1965). He later held a post at the University of Tokyo.
